{{short description|Polish mathematician (1915-2006)}}
[[File:Feliks Barański.jpg|thumb|upright=1.0|Feliks Barański]]
'''Feliks Barański''' (1915-2006) was a Polish [[mathematician]] and an active member of the so-called [[Lwów School of Mathematics]]. 

Born May 1915 in Lwów, [[Austria-Hungary]] (modern [[Lviv]], [[Ukraine]]), he joined the circle of young, talented mathematicians formed around [[Stefan Banach]] and [[Hugo Steinhaus]]. He obtained his [[doctorate]] under the supervision of [[Władysław Orlicz]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=51907&utm_source=copilot.com |title=Władysław Roman Orlicz |work=Mathematics Genealogy Project |access-date=25 July 2026}}</ref> During the period of German occupation of his hometown he made his living as a [[lice feeder]] in the institute of [[Rudolf Weigl]]. Expelled from Lwow after the war, he settled in [[Kraków]], where he joined the local [[Politechnika Krakowska|Kraków University of Technology]]. He was also admitted into the [[Polish Mathematical Society]].<ref>{{citation
 | last = Koroński | first = Jan
